subject: Model parameters and standard errors in underidentified model

messages.author: 8286cdcca1d3a44b
messages.subject: Model parameters and standard errors in underidentified model
parts:
Hello, 

I'm new to SEM/Lavaan and was wondering if I could get some guidance about this specific issue:

Does sem in Lavaan (sem(HS.model, data=mydata) compute the model parameters and standard errors even if the model is underidentified? or does it give errors? In other words does Lavaan perform an identification test while fitting the model or not?
If not, is there a way to find out whether the model is under identified in Lavaan?

Many thanks,
Karim

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Model parameters and standard errors in underidentified model
parts:
On 07/27/2014 12:14 AM, Karim Fawaz wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I'm new to SEM/Lavaan and was wondering if I could get some guidance
> about this specific issue:
>
> Does sem in Lavaan (sem(HS.model, data=mydata) compute the model
> parameters and standard errors even if the model is underidentified?

It will certainly try to compute the model parameters. But it will fail
to compute standard errors, and give you a warning about that.

If you do not need standard errors, you can set se="none"

> does Lavaan perform an
> identification test while fitting the model or not?

The 'identication' test is simply this: can we invert the information
matrix? If not, we may have (empirical) underidentification.

Yves.
